To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Wigner distribution may be computed from a multiple-shear spectral interference pattern, that this pattern may reveal sub-Planck-scale structure, and that the orientation of this structure may be arbitrary with respect to the canonical directions.

the Wigner distribution may be computed directly by measuring the multiple-shearing interference of an ultrashort pulse, and that the sub-Planchk-scale of the structure may also be extracted from the measured signal.

(1) the Wigner distribution is a useful tool for the characterization of the structure in a quantum state; (2) the structure in the quantum states of a photon may be on a sub-Planck spatial scale; (3) the structure on the quantum scale may be measured directly by using the analogy between the electric field of an ultrashort pulse and the wavefunction of the photon.

the measurement of the sub-quantum-scale structure in the phase space of a single photon.
measuring and visualizing the sub-Planchk scale structure of a quantum state.
